messages:
alan: Quick preflight for the cut today — aiming v2.19.0. Can folks confirm there are no left-behind PRs that need changelog entries or version bumps?
maya: I have a tiny docs-only PR, no code change and no changelog entry needed. will mark as docs. :white_check_mark:
jen: Two PRs from my side: "metrics/export: add env toggle" (has changelog entry in PR) and "batcher: minor perf tweak" (needs a version bump in setup.cfg). I'm about to push the version bump.
alan: Thanks. tagging rules: we prefer an annotated, signed tag and then create a draft GH release, upload artifacts (wheel, tar.gz), and attach checksums. I'll do the tag once final commit lands.
paul: Heads up — CI is still building the linux wheel for the batcher PR (artifact name: redwood_inference-2.19.0-py3-none-any.whl). ETA ~10m.
samir: I'm good on release notes. Can someone grep for any remaining "TODO: changelog" comments? I can sweep if you want.
jen: running: `git grep -n "TODO: changelog"` locally now. Nothing immediate.
alan: Perfect. small reminder about keys: I'll sign the tag with my GPG key (key id AB12CDEF). If that blocks anyone, ping me.
maya: :thumbsup: signed tags are good. Also please include the new quantization profile docs link in the release body.
alan: plan: 1) wait for CI artifacts, 2) merge remaining PRs, 3) create annotated signed tag `v2.19.0` and push, 4) create draft GH release with body, upload artifacts + checksums, 5) hand off to @release-bot to publish if all green.
paul: quick copy of commands I'll run for step 3/4: 
```
# create annotated signed tag
git tag -a v2.19.0 -m "v2.19.0 — batcher perf + metrics export" -s
git push origin v2.19.0

# create draft release with gh
gh release create v2.19.0 dist/*.whl dist/*.tar.gz --draft --title "v2.19.0" --notes-file RELEASE_NOTES.md
```

jen: For checksums I'll run `shasum -a 256 dist/* > dist/checksums.sha256` and upload that file too.
alan: good. Also attach the signed build provenance (if available) and note the quantization compatibility in the release notes.
samir: CI had an intermittent flake earlier on macos wheel build — if the mac wheel is busted we should still publish Linux wheels and mark macos as pending rather than block the release. Can we agree?
maya: agree with progressive publishing. as long as we document missing artifact and create a follow-up patch.
alan: OK that matches our rollback strategy. If mac wheel fails we'll: publish draft with linux artifacts, keep release as draft, and only publish final release once mac wheels are green OR we've added a post-release note.
release-bot: Draft release created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/releases/tag/v2.19.0 (status: draft) — artifacts pending upload.
paul: Uploaded linux wheel + tar.gz + checksums. pushed tag. `git push origin v2.19.0` succeeded.
jen: Verified checksums locally. DEPLOY_CHECKS: all passing except macos wheel.
alan: I'll review the draft notes, add the quantization docs link, and then request publish. If no objections by EOD I'll ask @release-bot to flip to published.
samir: LGTM from me.
maya: LGTM. thanks everyone. :rocket:
